tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. - "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). See Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ When `execute_code` is available, use it to read Datadog data, even for a single lookup: one script can make several API calls, join data across products, and return only what the answer needs. Skill guides still apply for domain knowledge (query syntax, attribute and metric names, pitfalls), but where a guide tells you to call a specific read tool such as `search_datadog_logs`, `analyze_datadog_logs`, or `get_datadog_metric`, make the equivalent call from `execute_code` instead, using `search_datadog_sdk` to find it. This takes precedence over tool choices in skill guides. Use the named tool only when `search_datadog_sdk` finds no operation for what you need, or when `execute_code` still fails for a step after following its own error guidance. This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).

{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjI2OTQwNTEx","is_bot":false,"login":"Beehtrix","name":""},"body":"### What happens

`recall --evidence` returns `<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>` text as `role: "user"` evidence when it is the content of a user turn. This happens with native claude-code records, both when `message.content` is a plain string and when it is a text block:

```json
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>"}}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>…</system-reminder>"}]}}
```

`docs/recall-evidence.md` (lines 42-43) says: "Structured hidden reasoning, tool output, system instructions and metadata are not returned as conversation text." That holds for system-role records, which the evidence path drops. It doesn't hold for reminder text inside a user turn.

The other conversation readers already skip these turns. In the run below, `conversationSubstantiveRequest` returns "" for both reminder lines, while the evidence path returns them as user spans. In that run the two reminder spans also came out ahead of the real user request.

### Repro

`main` @ f8deab17, Go 1.27.3, linux/amd64, run in a clean `env -i` with a throwaway HOME/GOPATH/GOCACHE. This is a throwaway test in `internal/cli` (not committed). It reuses the `evidenceFixture` setup from `recall_evidence_source_test.go`, writes one session with the lines below, and calls `collectEvidence(ctx, brain, "main", "zebrafoo", 10, 8192)`:

```
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"<system-reminder>zebrafoo string-form reminder</system-reminder>"}}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>zebrafoo block-form reminder</system-reminder>"}]}}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"please fix the zebrafoo parser"}]}}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Fixed the zebrafoo parser."}]}}
{"type":"system","content":"zebrafoo system-role record"}
```

Output:

```
state=available warnings=[] spans=4
EVIDENCE line=1 pointer=/message/content role="user" text="<system-reminder>zebrafoo string-form reminder</system-reminder>"
EVIDENCE line=2 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="user" text="<system-reminder>zebrafoo block-form reminder</system-reminder>"
EVIDENCE line=4 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="assistant" text="Fixed the zebrafoo parser."
EVIDENCE line=3 pointer=/message/content/0/text role="user" text="please fix the zebrafoo parser"
CONVERSATION line=1 conversationSubstantiveRequest=""
CONVERSATION line=2 conversationSubstantiveRequest=""
CONVERSATION line=3 conversationSubstantiveRequest="please fix the zebrafoo parser"
```

The system-role record on line 5 is dropped as expected. Lines 1 and 2 are returned as user evidence.

Compact v1 transcripts don't produce evidence on `main` at all yet. #564 adds that, and with #564 compact `<system-reminder>` user turns behave the same way. I didn't change that in #564 because this gap predates compact support.

### Expected (per the docs)

Wrapper or system-reminder text inside a user turn isn't returned as user conversation evidence, the same way system-role records aren't.

### Where in the code

- `internal/cli/recall_evidence_source.go:101-118`: the `content` helper in `evidenceJSONFields` adds every string or `text`/`input_text`/`output_text` block for `user`/`assistant` roles. Nothing checks the text.
- `internal/cli/recall_evidence_source.go:135-141`: the `user`/`assistant`/`message` case sends `message.content` through that helper.
- `internal/cli/conversation.go:292` and `:316`: the conversation reader skips `isWrapperRequest(text) || isConversationInjectedRequest(text)`. `isWrapperRequest` (`internal/cli/facts_eval_gen.go:646-655`) catches these turns because the text starts with `<`. `isConversationInjectedRequest` (`conversation.go:328`) only handles Stop-hook text. `history.go`, `reinforcement.go` and `facts_eval_gen.go` use `isWrapperRequest` too. The evidence path uses neither.

### Possible direction (your call)

One option is to skip user-role fields in `evidenceJSONFields` when the text matches the same wrapper predicate the other readers use. Another is a narrower check just for `<system-reminder>`-style wrappers. Note that `isWrapperRequest` drops any user text that starts with `<`, which may be broader than you want for evidence. The third option is to keep the behavior and change the docs to say that reminder text inside a user turn can show up. Which one fits the evidence contract is up to you.

Not checked: user turns that mix real text and a reminder in the same string or block list (only whole-field reminders were tested), other agents' wrapper formats, and the `recall --evidence` CLI end to end (the repro calls `collectEvidence` directly).

@evisdren @karthik-rameshkumar, I'm happy to take this if it's wanted. Could you assign it to me if so?

```md
Option 1 (apply isWrapperRequest to user-role fields in evidenceJSONFields) is the right one. It matches the behavior of every other reader, and Graph impact shows it is safe: evidenceJSONFields is only reached through evidenceFields → collectEvidence, so the filter is local to recall --evidence. isWrapperRequest itself has 24 production callers and would not change — the fix only adds a caller.```

The “drops any user text that starts with <” concern is real but already accepted: the conversation path has had the same tradeoff since it shipped. Evidence should not be stricter than conversation here.

Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".

## linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

The issue is still valid. I verified it on the current `main` tip (7de875e0) with the issue's own repro.

**Verification**
- I ran a throwaway test in `internal/cli` that reuses `evidenceFixture` and calls `collectEvidence` with the issue's five transcript lines. Both `<system-reminder>` user turns came back as `role: "user"` evidence, and both ranked ahead of the real request — the same output the issue shows. I deleted the test afterward; the worktree is clean.
- All code claims still hold, with small line shifts: the unfiltered `content` helper is now at `internal/cli/recall_evidence_source.go:101-118` inside `evidenceJSONFields` (93-158), the conversation readers still skip via `isWrapperRequest || isConversationInjectedRequest` (`conversation.go:292`, `:316`, `:793`), and `docs/recall-evidence.md` still has the "system instructions … are not returned" sentence.
- The two commits that touched `recall_evidence_source.go` since the issue (flat memory store, privacy-layer removal) did not add any filter. PR #564 (compact evidence) is still open, so its note is also current.

**Review of the proposed directions**
- Option 1 (apply `isWrapperRequest` to user-role fields in `evidenceJSONFields`) is the right one. It matches the behavior of every other reader, and Graph impact shows it is safe: `evidenceJSONFields` is only reached through `evidenceFields` → `collectEvidence`, so the filter is local to `recall --evidence`. `isWrapperRequest` itself has 24 production callers and would not change — the fix only adds a caller.
- The "drops any user text that starts with `<`" concern is real but already accepted: the conversation path has had the same tradeoff since it shipped. Evidence should not be stricter than conversation here.
- Option 2 (a narrower `<system-reminder>`-only check) would leave `<environment_context>` and other wrappers in, and would create a second predicate to maintain. Option 3 (docs change) keeps noise that outranks the real request, which defeats the feature.
- One scope note for the fix: the filter should apply per field, user role only. Assistant text that starts with `<` must stay. The codex `event_msg`/`user_message` path should get the same check.

I did not post anything to GitHub. The author (Beehtrix) asked to be assigned. If you want, I can post this review as an issue comment and you can assign them, or I can implement the fix here instead.

BODY:
Related to #412 and #534, and a companion to #560. **This PR is based on `main` and doesn't depend on #560.** It builds, passes and can merge either before or after #560 (details under "Relation to #560"). Not marked as fixing either issue, for the same reason as #560: #557 fixed the main symptom, and I don't know whether you consider those issues done.

The commits don't carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. I don't have a supported agent session to capture them from, and I didn't want to fake any.

## Why

Compact v1 records (`{"v":1,"type":"user"|"assistant","content":[...]}`, what the default export writes for claude-code, codex and pi) put the content at the record's top level, with no `message` wrapper. #557 taught the conversation, history-fragment and eval-gen readers to read that. Three more readers still look only inside `message`, and each one is broken on `main` (failing output below):

- **`episode_tools.go`**: `toolCallsFromObj` reads assistant content only from `message.content`. In a compact session it finds no `tool_use` blocks, so every episode has empty `ToolSequence` / `CommandSequence`. Episode segmentation on `main` already recognizes compact user turns, so the episodes exist but have no tools in them.
- **`pattern_corpus_enrich.go`**: `corpusEpisodeOps` has the same problem, so compact sessions add no `episode_tools`, `episode_commands` or file refs to the pattern corpus.
- **`recall_evidence_source.go`**: `evidenceJSONFields` produces no fields for compact records. Every compact session is marked `partial` with "contains unreadable or unsupported conversation content" and never returns an evidence span. Compact user text blocks also have no `type` (`{"text":"..."}`), and compact records keep the turn time in `ts`, not `timestamp`.

## What changed

- `episode_tools.go`, `pattern_corpus_enrich.go`: when a record has no `message` wrapper, read the assistant content from the top level. This is the same fallback `history.go` and `conversation.go` already use on `main`.
- `recall_evidence_source.go`: if a `user`/`assistant`/`message` record has no `message` key, its content is read from the top level with JSON pointers under `/content`, untyped `{"text":...}` blocks are accepted, and `ts` is used when `timestamp` is absent. All three only apply to records without a `message` key, so native claude-code, codex and opencode parsing is unchanged. Tool output (`tool_use.result`), images and thinking blocks are still excluded.
- `patterns.IndexerVersion` 9 → 10. The corpus skips a session when its size, mtime, sha and parser version are unchanged. A compact transcript's bytes don't change on upgrade, so without the bump, sessions already indexed with empty tool ops would stay that way. Earlier reader changes bumped this version the same way (see `docs/pattern_v2.md`).
- Episode projection versioned too. The bump above only reaches the SQLite corpus. `refreshPatternLayer` skips rebuilding `patterns/episodes.ndjson` (and the tasks, procedures and practices built from it) while the sessions fingerprint is unchanged, and an upgrade doesn't change it. The patterns source in the manifest now records `extraction_version` (the `patterns.IndexerVersion` that built the episodes), and `patternSourceCurrent` treats a different version as stale. Sources written before the field read as 0 and rebuild once. `patterns status` uses the same check, so it reports them `stale` until then.

Two commits: the reader fix with the version bump, then the episode-projection version and compact `ts`.

**Rebased onto current `main` (6c4b11de).** The only conflict was in `episodes.go`. #589 removed `PrivacyIdentity` from the pattern source. So `patternSourceCurrent` now compares only the sessions fingerprint and `ExtractionVersion`, and the `ExtractionVersion` it writes is just `patterns.IndexerVersion`. The commit message was updated to match.

## Relation to #560

#560 adds a `transcriptRecordContent` helper and compact fixtures in `history_compact_transcript_test.go`. This PR uses neither, so it doesn't depend on #560:

- The two tool-op readers use `main`'s existing inline fallback instead of the helper. If #560 merges, they can switch to `transcriptRecordContent` in a one-line follow-up.
- The fixtures live in `compact_transcript_ops_fixtures_test.go`, under different names (`compactOps{Claude,Codex,Pi}Transcript`), so the two PRs don't declare the same symbols. Their content is the same as #560's fixtures. Once both are in, one set can be deleted.
- Both PRs add an `ExtractionVersion` field to `internal/manifest`, but on different structs (`PatternSource` here, `HistorySource` in #560).

Checked against #560 rebased onto the same `main` (b7b4fb55): merging it with this branch is clean (git merge, no conflicts), and on the merged tree `go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1` passes. So it doesn't matter which one merges first.

## Tests

- `TestEpisodeToolSequencesCompactTranscript`, `TestBuildBrainEpisodesCompactTranscriptToolSequences` (the second goes through `buildBrainEpisodes`)
- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCompactTranscript`, `TestPatternCorpusReindexesCompactTranscriptToolOps`. The second builds the corpus, then models a v9 corpus (parser_version 9, tool ops deleted) and rebuilds.
- `TestRecallEvidenceCompactTranscript`: checks the exact fields per line, role and pointer. It also checks that every pointer resolves to the reported string in the source line, that no tool output leaks, and that each field's timestamp is the record's `ts`.
- `TestRefreshPatternLayerRebuildsEpisodesFromOlderExtractor`: builds the episode layer, rewrites it the way the old reader left it (same episodes, no tool ops, no `extraction_version`), then runs a normal (non-forced) `refreshPatternLayer`.

content.text:
Here is the overview of PR #564.

**The problem it fixes**

Compact v1 transcripts are the format the default export writes for claude-code, codex, and pi sessions. A compact record looks like `{"v":1,"type":"user","content":[...]}` — the content sits at the top level, with no `message` wrapper. PR #557 taught the main conversation and history readers to handle that shape, but three readers still looked only inside `message`. On `main`, each one silently failed on compact sessions:

1. **Episode tools** (`episode_tools.go`): episodes from compact sessions had empty tool and command sequences.
2. **Pattern corpus** (`pattern_corpus_enrich.go`): compact sessions added no tool ops or file refs to the pattern corpus.
3. **Recall evidence** (`recall_evidence_source.go`): every compact session was marked `partial` ("unreadable or unsupported") and returned no evidence spans.

**The fix**

- The two tool-op readers fall back to the record's top-level `content` when there is no `message` key. This copies the fallback `history.go` and `conversation.go` already use.
- The evidence reader does the same, and also accepts two compact quirks: text blocks with no `type` field, and the timestamp living in `ts` instead of `timestamp`. All of it applies only to records without a `message` key, so the native formats parse exactly as before.

**The cache-invalidation part** (the subtle half of the PR)

Fixing the readers is not enough. Both the pattern corpus and the episode layer skip rebuilds when the session files look unchanged — and a compact transcript's bytes do not change when the binary upgrades. So sessions already indexed with empty tool ops would stay wrong forever. The PR handles that twice:

- `patterns.IndexerVersion` bumps 9 → 10, which invalidates the SQLite corpus.
- The manifest's `PatternSource` gains an `extraction_version` field, and `patternSourceCurrent` treats a different version as stale. That forces one rebuild of `episodes.ndjson` and everything derived from it. Manifests written before the field read as version 0, so they rebuild once too.

**Tests**

Six new test functions cover all three readers, including a rebuild test that models an old v9 corpus and a stale episode layer. Each failure mode is pinned: the tests fail on unpatched `main`.

**What I changed to make it ready**

The PR predated #603, so one test still expected the compact fixture's `<system-reminder>` turn as user evidence. I merged current `main` in and removed that line — the planned one-line follow-up. Full suite, gofmt, and vet pass on the merged tree.

It now just needs CI green on head `e9855926`, then your approval.

# transcript

Package `github.com/entireio/cli/transcript` converts native agent transcripts
into the Entire Transcript Format and reads that format into typed Go values.

The library is versioned with CLI releases. Its API and the format may change;
consumers should pin a version.

## Entire Transcript Format v1

The format has been called the "compact transcript" (CLI code, metadata key
`compact_transcript`) and the "unified transcript" (entire-api). All three names
refer to the same thing. Stored names are unchanged: the file is
`transcript.jsonl`, the metadata key is `compact_transcript`, and the line field
is `cli_version`.

One JSON object per line, each line terminated by `\n`.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v` | int | yes | Always `1`. |
| `type` | string | yes | `user` or `assistant`. |
| `agent` | string | no | The CLI agent registry name (`claude-code`, `codex`, `copilot-cli`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `opencode`, `pi`, `antigravity`); otherwise the agent type string, e.g. for external agents. An open set. |
| `cli_version` | string | no | Version of the producer that wrote the line. The name is historical. |
| `ts` | string | no | Source timestamp where available, normally RFC 3339. May be omitted or empty when the native transcript has no timestamp. The generic JSONL converter copies source timestamps verbatim, so a non-string value can occur; readers ignore it. |
| `id` | string | no | Assistant message ID. Streaming fragments with the same ID are merged into one line. The Codex item path writes the item ID on user lines too. |
| `model` | string | no | Assistant lines only. The model the source reports for this call, verbatim; omitted when it reports none. Never inferred from a session-wide default, and never a placeholder: a value the agent writes in place of a model (Claude Code's `<synthetic>` on API-error entries) is omitted. |
| `input_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only. Input not counted in the line's `cache_read_tokens` or `cache_write_tokens`; see below. |
| `output_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only; includes reasoning tokens when the source reports them as part of output. |
| `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only; per-call cached input read and total cached input written. Cache counts are separate from fresh `input_tokens`. |
| `cache_write_5m_tokens`, `cache_write_1h_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only; an optional breakdown of `cache_write_tokens`, emitted only when the source reports the split (even when a reported value is zero). Absence means unknown, not zero or all 5m. Do not add the split to the total when summing usage. |
| `reasoning_tokens` | int | no | Assistant lines only; subset of `output_tokens` when reported by the source, not additional output. |
| `content` | array of blocks, string, or `null` | yes | Normally an array. A string can appear when an assistant message's source content was a string. `null` can appear because the writer does not omit empty content. |

Usage and model fields are per call, never copied from a session aggregate. A zero omitted by JSON encoding does not assert that the source reported zero.

On every line, `input_tokens` excludes the tokens in that line's `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`, so adding them never double counts. The sum is the call's total input only on lines from a converter that writes the cache fields. Lines written before that carry no cache fields, and their `input_tokens` is one of two things:

- Fresh input only (Claude Code, and Pi except as below): the cached input is missing from the line, so the sum understates the call's input.
- Fresh plus cached input (Codex, and Pi on Google models before pi-ai subtracted cached tokens in March 2026): the total is right, but its cache share is unknown, so pricing it at the fresh-input rate overstates the cost.

Other agents' lines copy the native input count as the agent defines it. Only `agent` and the `cli_version` that wrote a line tell these cases apart; no field marks a line as old or new, and `model` in particular says nothing about how `input_tokens` was counted.

Converters fill only what the native transcript reports per call. Claude Code, Codex and Pi record per-call usage and model, and their converters write them (below). Copilot CLI has only a shutdown aggregate, Cursor is hook-only, and external plugins and Antigravity report usage out of band, so their lines do not get these fields. Native timestamps are preserved where present; a missing one stays empty rather than fabricated.

### Per-call usage

An assistant line can carry usage with empty content (`"content":[]` or `"content":null`, for example an aborted or thinking-only call): readers that render transcripts should skip it, and readers that count usage must keep it.

Claude Code (`Options.Agent` `claude-code`, and `NewClaudeAdapter`; Cursor and Droid keep legacy counts): streaming fragments 

... [1150 characters truncated] ...

 (real order: call, output, `token_count`; outputs attach to their call by `call_id`). Usage is the difference between consecutive cumulative `info.total_token_usage` snapshots, and `ts` is the closing snapshot's when present, otherwise the last item's. Fresh input is `input - cached` clamped at zero; Codex lines carry no cache-write fields. Repeated snapshots and snapshots missing the input, cached-input or output counter are ignored, `reasoning_tokens` needs both adjacent snapshots to report it, and a decrease in any counter stops usage on later lines. A call with usage but no text or tool calls (for example reasoning-only) emits `content: []`, so consumers may see empty assistant lines; a call with neither usage nor content is omitted. Without usable `total_token_usage` snapshots (flat per-event totals are not read), no `token_count` closes a call, so consecutive assistant items merge into one line until the next user line or tool output; with usable snapshots, a tool output does not end its call. After a counter decrease, total snapshots still close calls but carry no usage, starting with the call the decrease closes. With `StartLine`, the last line before the boundary is part of the slice when its tool output or closing snapshot arrives after it (a one-line head overlap, which can repeat that call's usage); a later output for any earlier call lands only on that call's earlier line.

Codex, item path (current rollouts; see Blocks): one line per item, not per call. A call is the items up to the `token_count` that closes it, and its usage is computed exactly as on the `response_item` path: the same snapshot differences, fresh input, cached reads and reasoning, the model from `turn_context`, repeated snapshots ignored, and a counter decrease stopping usage. The usage goes on the call's last assistant line, so the call's earlier lines carry none. A call with usage but no assistant line (reasoning only) gets a usage-only line with `"content":null` and no `id`, whose `ts` is the closing snapshot's; other lines keep their item's `ts`. A user message ends the open call. With `StartLine`, the skipped lines seed the usage baseline, and the last line before the boundary is part of the slice when its call's closing snapshot arrives after it (a one-line head overlap).

Pi, one native message per call (no fragments to merge): `model` is `message.model`, and Pi's `input` is used as `input_tokens` unchanged, since the backends that report cached tokens already exclude them from it (a backend that folds cache reads into `input` cannot be told apart per call). `cache_write_1h_tokens` is Pi's `cacheWrite1h` and `cache_write_5m_tokens` the rest of `cacheWrite` (clamped at 0 if 1h exceeds it), only when Pi reports `cacheWrite1h`. `reasoning_tokens` is Pi's `reasoning` when reported. An assistant message with no visible content but non-zero usage (thinking-only, aborted) gets a line with `"content":null` (`"content":[]` before Pi went through the fold), so per-line usage sums to the session totals; one with zero usage gets none. Abandoned branches are excluded. Read per-call usage from the full converted transcript. Pi user `image` items pass through verbatim in Pi's native shape (`data`, `mimeType`) and in source order, so an image-only user message still has a line; `data` is the inline base64, or an `entire-asset:assets/…` placeholder when image externalization (`redaction.externalize_images`) moved the image to the checkpoint's assets.

### Blocks

- User text: `{"id"?: string, "text": string}`. There is no `type` field (a v1 quirk).
- Assistant text: `{"type": "text", "text": string}`.
- Tool use: `{"type": "tool_use", "id"?: string, "name": string, "input": any, "result"?: {"output": string, "status": "success"|"error", "file"?: {"filePath": string, "numLines"?: int}, "matchCount"?: int, "agent"?: {"id": string}}}`.
  Tool results are inlined into the `tool_use` block that requested them,
  matched by tool call ID where the agent records one, including the results
  of parallel calls that the agent writes separately.
  `agent.id` is the agent's own ID for the subagent session or thread the call
  launched (never the tool call ID, which is the block's `id`), when the parent
  transcript records one: Claude Code's `toolUseResult.agentId` (Agent, and
  forked Skill calls), Codex's `SubAgentActivity` thread for a `spawn_agent`
  call, OpenCode's `task` session (`state.metadata.sessionId`), and Copilot's
  `subagent.started` agent for a task call.
- Image: passed through from the source verbatim. The image source is either
  inline base64 or an `entire-asset:assets/…` placeholder left by image
  externalization.
- Any other block type is passed through verbatim. Thinking blocks are dropped
  by the converters.

Codex: rollouts from Codex versions that record items (the first turn has a
user message `item_completed` event) convert item by item: each
`item_completed` item becomes its own line or lines.

Pi user `image` items pass through verbatim in Pi's native shape (`data`, `mimeType`) and in source order, so an image-only user message still has a line; `data` is the inline base64, or an `entire-asset:assets/…` placeholder when image externalization (`redaction.externalize_images`) moved the image to the checkpoint's assets.

### Blocks

- User text: `{"id"?: string, "text": string}`. There is no `type` field (a v1 quirk).
- Assistant text: `{"type": "text", "text": string}`.
- Tool use: `{"type": "tool_use", "id"?: string, "name": string, "input": any, "result"?: {"output": string, "status": "success"|"error", "file"?: {"filePath": string, "numLines"?: int}, "matchCount"?: int, "agent"?: {"id": string}}}`.
  Tool results are inlined into the `tool_use` block that requested them,
  matched by tool call ID where the agent records one, including the results
  of parallel calls that the agent writes separately.
  `agent.id` is the agent's own ID for the subagent session or thread the call
  launched (never the tool call ID, which is the block's `id`), when the parent
  transcript records one: Claude Code's `toolUseResult.agentId` (Agent, and
  forked Skill calls), Codex's `SubAgentActivity` thread for a `spawn_agent`
  call, OpenCode's `task` session (`state.metadata.sessionId`), and Copilot's
  `subagent.started` agent for a task call.
- Image: passed through from the source verbatim. The image source is either
  inline base64 or an `entire-asset:assets/…` placeholder left by image
  externalization.
- Any other block type is passed through verbatim. Thinking blocks are dropped
  by the converters.

Codex: rollouts from Codex versions that record items (the first turn has a
user message `item_completed` event) convert item by item: each
`item_completed` item becomes its own line or lines.

content.text:
You're right that a canonical parser exists — but it lives in `entireio/cli`, not entiredb. The `entiredb` repo (entirehq org) is the storage service; it has no transcript parser.

**What exists: `github.com/entireio/cli/transcript`**
- Its README says it "converts native agent transcripts into the Entire Transcript Format and reads that format into typed Go values."
- It documents every quirk PR #564 just re-implemented by hand: user text blocks with no `type` field, the `ts` timestamp field, `null`/empty content, and `tool_use` blocks with inlined results.
- It is written for external consumers: "The library is versioned with CLI releases… consumers should pin a version." The API docs even note entire-api reads the same format.

**Why entire-brain doesn't use it today**
- entire-brain's `go.mod` has zero entireio dependencies. Nothing in Brain records a decision against importing it — recall returns no such memory. The closest recorded principle actually supports you: "the brain must reuse platform infrastructure rather than introduce its own."

**Where it would fit, and where it would not**
- The two tool-op readers (`episode_tools.go`, `pattern_corpus_enrich.go`) only need typed content blocks. They could use the library directly. Same for the conversation and history readers.
- The evidence reader is the hard one. Evidence spans address byte ranges in the original field string, and `content_sha256` binds that exact string, with a JSON pointer per field. A typed-value parser throws that positional information away. That reader would keep its own JSON walking, or the library would need a lower-level API.

**My recommendation**
- Merge #564 as-is. It is small, tested, and ready now.
- File a follow-up to adopt `entireio/cli/transcript` in the readers where typed values suffice, pinned to a CLI release. That removes the class of "one more reader missed the compact shape" bugs — this PR is the third such fix after #557 and #560.

Want me to file that follow-up issue on entire-brain?

gh issue create --repo entireio/entire-brain --title "Adopt entireio/cli/transcript for transcript readers instead of per-reader JSON handling" --body "## Why

Three PRs have now fixed the same class of bug: a reader that only understood the native \`message\`-wrapped record shape and silently failed on compact (ETF v1) transcripts — #557 (conversation, history-fragment, eval-gen readers), #560 (history compact readers), #564 (episode tools, pattern corpus, recall evidence). Each fix re-implements the same format knowledge by hand: top-level \`content\`, user text blocks with no \`type\` field, \`ts\` instead of \`timestamp\`, \`null\`/empty content.

A canonical parser already exists: \`github.com/entireio/cli/transcript\`. Its README documents every one of these quirks, reads ETF v1 into typed Go values, and is written for external consumers (\"versioned with CLI releases; consumers should pin a version\"). entire-api already reads the same format.

## Scope

Adopt the library in the readers where typed content blocks are sufficient:

- \`episode_tools.go\` (\`toolCallsFromObj\`)
- \`pattern_corpus_enrich.go\` (\`corpusEpisodeOps\`)
- the conversation / history readers where they duplicate ETF shape handling

Pin a CLI release in go.mod. This is entire-brain's first entireio dependency, so keep the import surface to the \`transcript\` package.

## Out of scope

\`recall_evidence_source.go\` keeps its own JSON walking. Evidence spans address byte ranges in the original field string, \`content_sha256\` binds that exact string, and each field carries a JSON pointer into the source line. A typed-value parser discards that positional information. Revisit only if the library grows a lower-level API that preserves source positions.

## Risks

- The library's API and the format can change between CLI releases; the pin must be bumped deliberately.
- Behavior differences between the library's reading and the current hand-rolled readers (for example thinking-block handling) need test coverage before the switch: the existing compact-transcript tests from #557/#560/#564 should pass unchanged." 2>&1 | tail -1

Fixes #566, fixes #567

## Why

This fixes compact codex `apply_patch` file refs. I asked on #566 to be assigned and haven't heard back yet. If someone else is already on this, I'm happy to close it.

**This depends on #564.** It's stacked on #564's current head (`ebf7c6c8`, which is on `main` `6c4b11de`). Until #564 merges, this PR's diff also shows #564's two commits. The rest are new: `24b55dbe` for #566, the two commits from #602 (`bb1a698b`, `02d16560`) and `1afc32da` for #567, plus two merges of `main`. I'll rebase onto `main` once #564 lands. It can't stand alone on `main`: compact records never reach `claudeContentOps` there, and the compact fixtures come from #564. Against current `main` (`fb99b029`) the branch merges cleanly (`git merge-tree`) and the full suite passes on the merge (see Tests).

A compact v1 codex `apply_patch` `tool_use` has no path field. For older Codex rollouts the cli converter (its `response_item` path) wraps the `custom_tool_call` patch text as `{"input": <patch>}` (`codexCustomToolUseBlock`, entireio/cli `transcript/codex.go`). `claudeContentOps` only looked at `file_path` / `path` / `filename`, so the block gave no file refs. The same patch from a native `custom_tool_call` gives one ref per `*** Add/Update/Delete File` line. That left a patch-only compact turn with no write ref, so `classifyEpisodeShape` labelled it `read_only`, which also made it eligible for themes.

## What changed

- `internal/cli/pattern_corpus_enrich.go`: if `apply_patch` has no path, `claudeContentOps` now runs `patchFiles` on `input.input`, the same helper the native `custom_tool_call` case uses. An explicit path still takes priority. (+5 lines)
- `internal/cli/patterns/runs.go`: `IndexerVersion` 10 → 11 (#564 takes it 9 → 10). The corpus skips a session when its size, mtime, sha and parser version are all unchanged, and a compact transcript's bytes don't change on upgrade, so without the bump sessions indexed by the version 10 reader would keep their missing file refs and `read_only` shapes.

### Versions and #575

I kept this in line with #575's approach (wire/schema versions stay readable by stable clients; only an extractor revision moves):

- Only `patterns.IndexerVersion` changes. Through #564 the same constant is the patterns source's `extraction_version` in the manifest, so the episode projection rebuilds once; `corpusEpisodeOps` is only called by the corpus indexer, so `episodes.ndjson` comes out the same.
- No schema version changes, and the history scan cache is not touched (`historyScanCacheVersion` / `historyScanCacheWireVersion` from #575 stay as they are): `claudeContentOps` is only reached from `corpusEpisodeOps`, which the history scan doesn't use.
- One thing for #564 rather than this PR: `extraction_version` is a new field in the manifest, and a pre-#564 build's manifest writer decodes strictly, so after a #564+ build refreshes a brain, an older build sharing it refuses to rewrite the manifest (run on `main` `fb99b029`: tolerant read drops the field; strict write path returns "brain manifest carries a field this build does not know (json: unknown field "extraction_version")"). This PR only changes the value, not whether the field is there.

## Ordering with the #567 fix

This PR also carries the #567 fix (below), folded in from #602 as evisdren suggested on #567, so `patterns.IndexerVersion` is bumped once (10 → 11).

## Tests

- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCompactTranscript`: the codex row #564 pinned as `files: nil` now expects `edit internal/cli/export.go`.
- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCompactApplyPatchMatchesNative` (new): one patch with Add, Update and Delete. Native and compact must give the same refs (`add docs/new.md,edit internal/cli/export.go,delete old.go`), and `apply_patch` with an explicit `path` still gives just that path.
- `TestPatternCorpusCompactApplyPatchShapesWrite` (new): goes through `buildPatternCorpus` with #564's codex fixture. The episode shapes must be `0:shell,1:write` and `episode_files` must have the edit. It then models a version 10 corpus (`parser_version=10`, file refs deleted), rebuilds, and checks that both are back.

# Changelog

All notable changes to `entire-brain` are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- `recall --evidence` no longer returns harness-injected `<system-reminder>`
  text as `role: "user"` evidence. User-role strings and text blocks now go
  through the same wrapper filter as the conversation reader, so reminders,
  `Caveat:` notes and environment envelopes are skipped like system-role
  records already were. As in conversation, user text that itself starts with
  `<` is skipped too. Assistant text is unchanged (#565).

## [0.5.1] - 2026-11-04

### Fixed

- Give waiting foreground writers priority over background work. Watchers,
  memory workers, and detached backfills wait without spending job retries on
  writer contention. Active atomic writes finish before another writer starts.
- Fetch and filter hosted memories outside the writer lock. Recheck the feed
  cache and connection before committing, and preserve concurrent local writes.
- Limit hosted pull retries when concurrent syncs keep changing the feed cache.
  Wait briefly between attempts, and allow cancellation during that wait.
- Preserve completed distillation results and cache entries when cancellation
  interrupts a wait for the writer lock.
- Avoid re-reading the complete memory store when updating the manifest after
  `remember` or a hosted pull. Storage and hosted wire formats remain unchanged.

- Remove verified redundant legacy memory files automatically during normal
  writes and refreshes, and during unchanged watcher passes. This also covers
  copies retained by v0.5.0. Repository and global stores need no cleanup command.
- Verify complete migrated records before cleanup. Preserve unrecognized or
  unverified data, and resume interrupted cleanup from durable verification
  receipts. Large-file verification runs outside the brain write lock.
- Report pending cleanup, retained recovery data, and recorded reclaimed bytes
  through `memories storage status --json`. Reads remain read-only. Background

Related to #412 and #534. Not marked as fixing them: #557 already fixed the main symptom (compact transcripts reading as empty), and I don't know whether you consider those issues done.

This is rebased onto `main` 6c4b11de and merges cleanly with current `main` (fb99b029). That brings in #575's split scan-cache versions, #589's privacy-layer removal and #590's flat fact store. I adjusted the versioning to fit, as described below. If you'd rather not take it, or want it split, say so and I'll adjust or close it.

The commits don't carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers: I don't have a supported agent session to capture them from, and I didn't want to fake any.

## What #557 already does

It reads top-level `content` for compact records in the conversation, history-fragment and eval-gen readers. Two of my new tests (`TestScanConversationCompactTranscript`, `TestHistoryIndexesDefaultCompactExport`) pass on unmodified main.

## What this PR still adds

Three of my new tests still fail on main 6c4b11de (re-run after the rebase): `TestExtractHistoryJSONFragmentsCompactTranscript`, `TestHistoryIndexBuildsRecordsFromCompactTranscript` and `TestHistoryDeltaRescansOverlayFromPreCompactReader`.

- **Tool output in code facts.** Compact transcripts inline tool output as `tool_use.result.output`, with no separate `tool_result` record. `extractContentFragments` now mines it, so compact sessions get code facts. Native transcripts have no `result` key, so nothing changes for them.
- **Rebuild stale history indexes.** The history source manifest stores `extraction_version`, and `historyIndexCurrent` treats an index built with another version as stale. Without it, a plain `refresh` with unchanged transcripts keeps an index built by an older reader. Manifests from older binaries have no field, read as 0 and rebuild once.
- **Scan cache: only the extractor revision moves.** #575 split the scan cache into a wire version (10, which released clients still read) and `extractor_version`. This PR moves only the extractor revision, `historyScanCacheVersion` 11 → 13. `historyScanCacheWireVersion` stays 10.
  - Revision 12 mines compact tool output, because a revision-11 cache holds scans with no code facts.
  - Revision 13 covers the null/empty `message` fallback below. Earlier builds of this branch wrote revision 12 without that fallback, and their caches would otherwise stay current. I confirmed this with a run: a brain built by one of those builds kept 0 exchanges after a refresh at revision 12, and gets 2 at 13 (`TestHistoryRefreshRescansRevision12NullMessageCache`, with a real fixture).
  - `TestHistoryScanCacheWireCompatibilityAndExtractionInvalidation` follows the constant now.
  - `TestHistoryScanCachePreviousExtractorRevisionRescans` checks that a cache from the previous revision is rescanned rather than reused.
  - `docs/memory-storage-compatibility.md` now says revision 13.
- **Short-term overlay: format stays 3 and gains `extractor_version`.** An earlier version of this PR bumped `historyShortTermVersion` 3 → 4 instead. That made every existing v3 overlay load as unsupported on upgrade, so recent sessions held only in the overlay fell back to the long-term index until the next delta. A build without the change also couldn't read a v4 overlay. I confirmed both by running them. Now the overlay keeps format 3 and records the extraction revision. A delta carries an unchanged file's entry forward only when the overlay's `extractor_version` matches the current revision. So an old overlay with an empty entry for a compact transcript is still readable, and that file is re-parsed on the next delta. Removing the reuse check, or not writing the field, each makes `TestHistoryDeltaRescansOverlayFromPreCompactReader` fail. Until that delta runs, the overlay doesn't count as complete coverage. Otherwise `doctor` would say "short-term memory covers the gap" for entries an older extractor built. Instead it reports partial coverage and names `refresh delta`, which `TestShortTermOverlayStatesNeverClaimCoverage` checks.
  - Only earlier builds of this branch ever wrote version 4 (no main commit or release did). Such an overlay has the v3 layout without `extractor_version`, so it's now read as v3 with an unknown extractor: it stays in retrieval, isn't counted as complete, and the next delta rewrites it as v3. Before this, the overlay loaded as unsupported and doctor said to upgrade. `TestHistoryShortTermReadsLegacyV4Overlay` uses a real overlay written by one of those builds. Version 4 is reserved now, so the "unknown newer overlay" health test uses 5.
- **Doctor flags an index from an older extractor.** `history_freshness` used to compare only session fingerprints, so it said "built from the current exported sessions" for an index that `refresh` would rebuild. It now warns and names `refresh` (`TestDoctorHistoryFreshnessFlagsOlderExtractor`). The warning, and the overlay's partial-coverage text, give the revision and say whether it's older or newer than this binary's. Before, data from a newer binary was also called "older". Behaviour is unchanged: any other revision is re-parsed, as with the scan cache.
- **One shared helper.** `transcriptRecordContent` returns a `user`/`assistant` record's content in either shape (nested under `message`, otherwise top-level `content`). It replaces the separate fallbacks #557 added in each reader. Those fallbacks disagreed on an edge case: `"message":{}` or `null`. A null or empty `message` now counts as absent, and `TestTranscriptRecordContentPrecedence` pins the order.

## Commits

1. fix(history): read compact v1 transcripts in history and conversation readers

- **Doctor flags an index from an older extractor.** `history_freshness` used to compare only session fingerprints, so it said "built from the current exported sessions" for an index that `refresh` would rebuild. It now warns and names `refresh` (`TestDoctorHistoryFreshnessFlagsOlderExtractor`). The warning, and the overlay's partial-coverage text, give the revision and say whether it's older or newer than this binary's. Before, data from a newer binary was also called "older". Behaviour is unchanged: any other revision is re-parsed, as with the scan cache.
- **One shared helper.** `transcriptRecordContent` returns a `user`/`assistant` record's content in either shape (nested under `message`, otherwise top-level `content`). It replaces the separate fallbacks #557 added in each reader. Those fallbacks disagreed on an edge case: `"message":{}` or `null`. A null or empty `message` now counts as absent, and `TestTranscriptRecordContentPrecedence` pins the order.

# Changelog

All notable changes to `entire-brain` are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- `recall --evidence` no longer returns harness-injected `<system-reminder>`
  text as `role: "user"` evidence. User-role strings and text blocks now go
  through the same wrapper filter as the conversation reader, so reminders,
  `Caveat:` notes and environment envelopes are skipped like system-role
  records already were. As in conversation, user text that itself starts with
  `<` is skipped too. Assistant text is unchanged (#565).

Fixes #600. @evisdren, this uses the two defaults from my comment on #600, and I'm happy to switch either one. Fork pre-review: Beehtrix/entire-brain#23

Builds on #601 (merged): it changes what #601's `compactCodexExitCodes` does for `Bash` blocks, and takes `IndexerVersion` one step past #601's 11. The branch starts from #601's head, so the diff is only this PR's five commits.

## Why

Since entireio/cli#2897 (shipped in cli 0.13.1), the cli converts a current Codex rollout through its items. Two things it writes weren't read:

- A failed command is a compact `Bash` block with `result.status:"error"`. Its output is the command's own, with no exit text, and the rollout's `exit_code` isn't carried over. The corpus stored it as `exit_code=NULL, failed=0`, so it was missing from `exit_fails`.
- An edit is a `FileChange` block with `input.changes[].path` (absolute) and `kind`. It gave no file ref, so a turn whose only edit was a `FileChange` had no write ref.

## The two defaults

1. **A `Bash` block with status `"error"` is stored as failed, with `exit_code` NULL.** It counts in `exit_fails`. This is only for compact codex `Bash` blocks; claude-code and pi `status:"error"` are still not read (that's #567's open question). The cli writes `"error"` when an item failed **or was declined** ([`codexitem.Item.Failed`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/3a760b96a60fe1bf68f70bc1c164257df7b43e9e/internal/transcript/codexitem/item.go#L84-L91), used at [`codex_items.go#L78`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/3a760b96a60fe1bf68f70bc1c164257df7b43e9e/transcript/codex_items.go#L75-L80)), so a command the user declined counts as failed too. The compact record can't tell them apart. If that's wrong, the other way is for the cli to carry the exit code (or the declined status) in the compact result.
2. **A `FileChange` path is stored relative to the repo root of the session that wrote it.** The session's checkpoint already records the files it touched relative to the repo (`files_touched`), so a candidate root is what's left of a `FileChange` path once a touched file is stripped from its end: `/home/ada/src/repo/cmd/main.go` with `cmd/main.go` touched gives `/home/ada/src/repo`. A candidate scores one for each distinct session path that is a touched file under it, and the highest score wins, so a checkout named like one of its own directories or repeated edits of one file can't pick the wrong root. Every path under the winner is stored relative to it, so the ref links to symbols the way an `apply_patch` path does. A path outside the root is kept as written, as a Claude `file_path` is today. So is every path of a session whose touched files match none of them or whose top score is tied, since a wrong root would link edits to the wrong files, and so is any path with a `..` segment, since the OS resolves `..` after symlinks. A session with such a path gets no root at all, since leaving it out could hand the root to the rest. The other way is for the cli to write repo-relative paths (it knows the rollout's `cwd`).

The second default goes further than my comment on #600 said. Because the root comes from the session rather than from the checkout building the corpus, a session from a sibling worktree or a teammate's machine is made relative too, and the stored refs are the same whichever checkout runs `refresh`.

`kind` maps `add`, `delete` and `update` to `add`, `delete` and `edit`; any other kind is an `edit`. An `update` with a `move_path` is a `delete` of the old path plus an `add` of the new one. Like an `apply_patch`, a change counts whatever its result status.

## What changed

- `pattern_corpus_enrich.go`: `compactCodexExitCodes` becomes `compactCodexResults`, which also records a `Bash` block's status `"error"` as a failure with no exit code. `claudeContentOps` reads `FileChange` changes (`fileChangeFiles`). `codexSessionRoot` infers a session's root from its `FileChange` paths and `files_touched`, and `repoRelativePath` makes a path under that root relative. Both accept `/` and `\` separators. Scores are counted in one pass over each path's `/` splits, so a long session stays linear.
- `pattern_corpus.go`: `indexSessionIntoCorpus` infers the root once per session and passes it to `corpusEpisodeOps`. Since the root comes from the checkpoint's `files_touched`, `corpusSessionUnchanged` also compares the checkpoint a session was exported from (the `checkpoint_id` already in `indexed_sessions`), so a later checkpoint of the same transcript re-indexes it.
- `patterns/runs.go`: `IndexerVersion` 11 → 12. The transcript bytes don't change on upgrade, so only the bump makes the next build re-index these sessions instead of skipping them as unchanged.
- `docs/pattern_v2.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` (under Unreleased).

## Tests

New, in `pattern_corpus_codex_items_test.go`:

- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCodexItemPathCommands`: status `"error"` is failed with no exit code, even with exit text in the output; status `"success"` that prints `Exit code: 1` or `exited with code 1` is not failed (moved from #601's test); a block with no result yet is not failed.
- `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCodexItemPathFileChange`: update, add, delete, move, unknown kind, a relative path, a path outside the root, a sibling directory that shares the root's prefix, an empty path, a Windows path, `.` segments cleaned, `..` paths inside and leaving the root kept as written, and no root known.
- `TestCodexSessionRoot`: one touched file, untouched paths following the session's root, a checkout named like one of its own directories, repeated edits of one file counting once, the root most paths agree on, a `move_path`, Windows paths, a `./` spelling, `.` segments and doubled slashes, and no root when one path ends in two touched files, two roots tie (nested, or unrelated with more paths), any path or `move_path` has `..`, nothing is touched, nothing matches, the paths are relative, or there's no `FileChange`.
- `TestPatternCorpusIndexesCodexItemPath`: through `buildPatternCorpus` with a live graph context, for a session recorded under `/home/teammate/src/repo` (not the checkout building the corpus) with `files_touched: ["main.go"]`. The failed `go test` gives `failed=1 exit_fails=1`, the `FileChange` of `/home/teammate/src/repo/main.go` is stored as `main.go`, links to its 2 symbols, and makes the turn a `write`. Then a corpus reset to indexer version 11 is re-indexed on the next build.
- `TestPatternCorpusReindexesCodexSessionForNewCheckpoint`: a session first indexed with no `files_touched` keeps its absolute path; moving it to a new checkpoint with `files_touched: ["main.go"]`, transcript untouched, re-indexes it to `main.go` with its 2 symbols. It fails without the checkpoint comparison.

Updated: `TestCorpusEpisodeOpsCompactNonCodexResultsLeftAlone` (from #601) now covers only claude-code and pi, since the codex item-path case it pinned is what this PR changes. The other corpus op tests pass `""` for the new `repoRoot` argument, and the episode test fixture can now set `files_touched` and rewrite only its manifest.

### Before / after

With `IndexerVersion` left at 11, the rebuild check fails:

```
--- FAIL: TestPatternCorpusIndexesCodexItemPath (0.07s)
    version 11 corpus kept its missing failure and file ref after rebuild: corpus = "go test exit_code=<nil> failed=0 exit_fails=0 files= refs= shape=shell symbols=0", want "go test exit_code=<nil> failed=1 exit_fails=1 files=[\"main.go\"] refs=edit main.go shape=write symbols=2"
```

With the change, it and the other new tests pass.

### End to end through the real cli converter

On entireio/cli `main` @ `3a760b96` (the 0.13.1 changelog commit), a throwaway test (not committed) passed a hand-written rollout to `transcript.Convert(..., Options{Agent: "codex"})`: a `CommandExecution` with `status:"failed"` and `exit_code:1`, one with `status:"declined"`, a `FileChange` of `/work/repo/main.go` (update), `/work/repo/docs/new.md` (add) and `/work/repo/a/old.go` moved to `/work/repo/b/new.go`, then a passing command. A throwaway brain test read the output with `corpusEpisodeOps(..., "/work/repo")`:

```
tools=["bash" "bash" "filechange" "bash"]
commands=["go test exit=nil failed=true","rm exit=nil failed=true","go test exit=nil failed=false"]
files=["delete a/old.go","add b/new.go","add docs/new.md","edit main.go"]
```

The second command is the declined one.

## What was run and what was only read

Run on linux/amd64 with Go 1.27.2: `gofmt -l -s .` (clean), `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/cli/`, the corpus tests under `-race`, and `go test ./... -count=1`. That full run has 4 failures in `internal/cli` that fail the same way on #601's head without this change, so they come from my environment, not from this PR: `TestRunDistillForBrainSurvivesMidRunFlushFailure`, `TestShortTermOverlayStatesNeverClaimCoverage`, `TestSemanticIndexReportsReadOnlyBrainDirectory`, `TestHistoryLegacyIdentityNoPayloadCorruptPayloadAndReadOnlyFailOpen`.

Read, not run: Windows and macOS (the path handling is plain string work on `/`, with `\` converted first, and Windows paths are in the tests, but the suite wasn't run on either), real captured Codex sessions (the rollout above is hand-written in the shape of the cli's own fixtures), and the other readers of compact tool blocks (recall evidence, episode tools), which #600 left out of scope.

content.text:
**PR #612 — latest state and review verdict: code is solid, but it is waiting on a product call from you, not on code.**

**State**
- Open, head `5258aecc`, slightly behind `main` — it merges cleanly (only #609's CHANGELOG entries come in), so no rebase is strictly needed.
- CI has not run on this head — the fork workflow run needs your approval. Codex bot review: completed, no findings.
- My local validation on the PR merged with current `main`: full `go test ./... -count=1` passes, gofmt and vet clean. The four failures the author saw are their environment — all four tests pass here.

**What it does** — fixes #600: current-Codex (item-path) sessions now record command failures (`status:"error"` → `failed=1`, exit code NULL) and `FileChange` file refs, with the repo root inferred per session from the checkpoint's `files_touched`, so absolute paths become repo-relative on any machine. `IndexerVersion` 11 → 12 re-indexes once.

**The decision blocking merge:** the author explicitly asks you to confirm two defaults, and my review agrees the first one matters: the cli writes `"error"` for both a failed command and one the user **declined**, so a declined command is stored as a real failure and counts in `exit_fails`. The compact record cannot tell them apart. Accept that (with the cli carrying a declined marker later), or ask for a different default.

**Non-blocking findings from my structured review**, worth passing to the author or deferring:
- A `FileChange` change with an empty `path` but a set `move_path` is dropped entirely — the added file gets no ref. Small genuine edge bug.
- A new checkpoint re-indexes a session even when `files_touched` is unchanged (comparing `checkpoint_id` instead of a fingerprint) — churn, not corruption.
- The two FileChange walkers disagree on case/block-type matching; one shared walker would fix it.
- The ~130-line root heuristic is a stopgap for the cli not writing `cwd`/repo-relative paths — worth a cli-repo follow-up issue so it can eventually be deleted.
- A repo mounted at filesystem root `/` can never infer a root. Rare.

My suggestion: answer the #600 defaults question (accepting default 1 is defensible), ask for the empty-path/`move_path` fix since it is a two-line change, approve CI, and treat the rest as follow-ups. Want me to post that as a review comment on the PR?

gh pr comment 612 --repo entireio/entire-brain --body "Review result — answering the #600 defaults question and noting one small fix I pushed.

**Default 1 (a \`Bash\` block with status \`error\` is stored as failed, exit code NULL, counts in \`exit_fails\`): accepted**, including the declined-command ambiguity. A declined command ends the loop the same way a failing one does, and the compact record can't tell them apart today. The right long-term fix is the cli carrying the exit code or a declined marker in the compact result — worth filing on entireio/cli; if that lands, this default can be revisited without another IndexerVersion ceremony since the field would be new data.

**Default 2 (FileChange paths stored relative to the session's own root, inferred from \`files_touched\`): accepted.** Deriving the root from the session rather than the building checkout is the right call for shared corpora across worktrees and machines.

**Pushed directly** (maintainer edit, \`5eb4755c\`): a change with kind \`update\`, an empty \`path\` and a set \`move_path\` was dropped before the move branch ran, so the added file got no ref. The move branch now runs first and emits the add; the delete is skipped when there is no old path. One test case added.

**Noted as follow-ups, no change requested here:**
- The two FileChange walkers differ (case-sensitive \`\"FileChange\"\` + any block type in \`codexFileChangePaths\` vs lowercased name + \`tool_use\`/\`tool\` in \`claudeContentOps\`). Harmless against today's converter; a shared walker would remove the asymmetry. Fits #613's adoption of the cli transcript package.
- Comparing \`checkpoint_id\` re-indexes a session on every new checkpoint even when \`files_touched\` is unchanged. A fingerprint of \`files_touched\` would invalidate exactly on the input that matters.
- A repo checked out at filesystem root \`/\` can never infer a root (the scoring loop starts at the second byte). Rare container case.
- The root heuristic as a whole is a good stopgap; the structural fix is the cli writing \`cwd\` or repo-relative paths.

Full \`go test ./... -count=1\`, gofmt and vet pass locally on this head merged with current main. The four \`internal/cli\` failures mentioned in the PR body don't reproduce here — all four pass, so they do look environment-specific." 2>&1 | tail -1
